title: Serving, Testing & Monitoring ML
why: A model in a notebook is not a product. Shipping and maintaining models is what separates ML engineers from experimenters.
explain: Serving means packaging the model together with its preprocessing, exposing a stable interface (REST, gRPC or a batch job), validating inputs and meeting latency and reliability targets. Training/serving skew, where training and production compute features differently, is a top cause of silent failures, so share one code path for both.

Test ML systems at several levels: unit tests for transforms, data validation (schema and ranges), model tests (minimum accuracy on a golden set, invariance checks) and API contract tests. Version code, data and models so any prediction can be reproduced, and run the checks in CI.

In production, monitor latency, errors, input drift (for example the population stability index or a KS test) and outcome quality once labels arrive. Have a rollback plan, use shadow or canary deployments, and cache repeated requests where it is safe.
key_points: One shared code path for training and serving features
Validate inputs at the API boundary
Test data, transforms, the model and the API separately
Monitor drift as well as latency and errors
Canary or shadow deployments with a rollback plan
pitfalls: Loading a pickled model from an untrusted source (arbitrary code execution)
Monitoring only uptime and never the quality of predictions

leetcode.why: LRU caching is the standard answer for speeding up repeated predictions.
Time-versioned storage models feature stores and point-in-time correctness.
Scheduling tasks with cooldowns resembles batch-job and rate-limit planning.
Merging per-user event streams with heaps is the core of feed and timeline ranking services.

industry.q: What is training/serving skew and how do you prevent it?
key_points: Features computed differently offline and online
Share the same transformation code or use a feature store
Log served features and compare with training distributions
Add integration tests on a golden dataset

industry.q: How do you detect and respond to data drift?
key_points: Compare live feature distributions with training (PSI, KS test)
Monitor the prediction distribution and delayed labels
Alert thresholds with retrain or rollback triggers
Separate covariate drift from concept drift

industry.q: Design an API that serves a fraud model at 2,000 requests per second with p99 latency under 50 ms.
key_points: Stateless replicas behind a load balancer with the model held in memory
Observability, canary releases and load tests
